title: Search & Retrieval
lead: Hybrid BM25 + vector retrieval tuned for 100% recall.
summary: MemPalace fuses vector semantic search with keyword-based BM25 scoring and optional closet-boosting to approach perfect retrieval. The system reaches 96.6% R@5 with zero LLM, 98.4% R@5 on held-out data through the full hybrid pipeline, and optional Haiku reranking pushes that to 100%. A weak semantic match can always be rescued by strong keyword overlap or temporal/preference signals, eliminating the pure-vector cold-retrieval problem. Vector candidate selection is the floor that always runs; later steps can only improve ranking, never suppress a result.

concepts.definition: Probabilistic keyword matching algorithm that scores documents based on term frequency and inverse document frequency (IDF), tuned with k1=1.5 and b=0.75 per standard conventions.

Vector similarity metric in the [0, 2] range used by ChromaDB's HNSW index; 0 = identical vectors, 2 = opposite. MemPalace interprets it as absolute distance (not relative-to-max) to ensure stable ranking under candidate addition/removal.
Convex combination of vector similarity (60% weight) and normalized BM25 score (40% weight) applied at re-rank time. Candidates are scored as: 0.6 * vec_sim + 0.4 * bm25_norm, then sorted.

Ranking signal where a matching closet (topic index layer) reduces the effective distance of drawers from its source file by 4-40% depending on closet rank, clamped to [0, 2] to preserve cosine invariants.
Policy for gathering candidates before hybrid re-rank: 'vector' (default) uses top n_results*3 from HNSW; 'union' also pulls BM25-only candidates from SQLite FTS5 to widen the re-rank pool.
The distance after closet boost is applied: max(0.0, min(2.0, raw_dist - boost)), ensuring the result stays in valid cosine range [0, 2].
When a closet-boosted match spans multiple chunks in a source file, the system selects the chunk with the highest keyword-term overlap and returns it plus immediate neighbors for context.
SQLite FTS5-based search used when HNSW vector index is corrupted or unloadable, enabling graceful degradation to keyword search without segfaulting the server.

symbols.name: search_memories
symbols.role: Main programmatic search API used by MCP server and other callers; returns a dict instead of printing. Handles vector-only, BM25-only fallback, and union-candidate strategies.

symbols.name: _hybrid_rank
symbols.role: Re-ranks candidates by convex combination of vector similarity (60%) and BM25 (40%), handling both vector-aware and vector-unknown candidates. Mutates results in-place.

symbols.name: _bm25_scores
symbols.role: Computes Okapi-BM25 scores for a query against a document corpus, using Lucene/BM25+ smoothed IDF formula over the candidate set.

symbols.name: _merge_bm25_union_candidates
symbols.role: Appends BM25-only candidates from SQLite into the rerank pool when candidate_strategy='union', with chunk-precise dedup.

symbols.name: sanitize_query
symbols.role: Extracts actual search intent from potentially contaminated queries using 4-step fallback (passthrough, question extraction, tail sentence, tail truncation).

symbols.name: get_embedding_function
symbols.role: Returns cached embedding function bound to user-selected device and model (minilm or embeddinggemma). Falls back gracefully if requested accelerator unavailable.

symbols.name: EmbeddinggemmaONNX
symbols.role: ChromaDB-compatible embedding function using embeddinggemma-300m ONNX quantized; multilingual, lazy-loaded from HuggingFace.

symbols.name: dedup_palace
symbols.role: Main entry point for deduplicating near-identical drawers within source groups using cosine-distance threshold; supports dry-run and selective scoping.

symbols.name: check_text
symbols.role: Fact-checking API that detects entity-name confusion (edit distance <=2), relationship mismatches, and stale facts against the knowledge graph.

symbols.name: CLOSET_RANK_BOOSTS
symbols.role: [0.40, 0.25, 0.15, 0.08, 0.04] - ordinal boost values for closet ranks 0-4, applied as distance reduction to drawer results from matching sources.

surprises.title: Raw verbatim text baseline beats extraction-based systems by 2x
surprises.detail: MemPalace's baseline (96.6% R@5 on LongMemEval with zero LLM) outperforms Mem0's LLM-extracted memories by over 2x. Extraction loses context: when Mem0 extracts 'user prefers PostgreSQL' and discards the conversation, it loses why they prefer it, what alternatives were considered, and what they'd said before. MemPalace stores everything verbatim and lets search find it.

surprises.title: Closet boosts use rank, not absolute distance, as the signal
surprises.detail: CLOSET_RANK_BOOSTS = [0.40, 0.25, 0.15, 0.08, 0.04] uses the closet's ordinal position, not its absolute distance, to decide boost magnitude. Narrative content produces closet distances in the 1.2-1.5 range regardless of match quality, making absolute distance unreliable. Rank is more stable. Distances > 1.5 bypass boosts entirely (CLOSET_DISTANCE_CAP).

surprises.title: Absolute cosine similarity prevents ranking instability under candidate changes
surprises.detail: Vector similarity is computed as max(0, 1 - distance), using absolute distance not relative-to-max. Adding/removing a candidate cannot reshuffle other candidates. If similarity were (max_dist - dist) / max_dist, adding a very-close result would increase max_dist and reshuffle all other scores. Absolute scoring is essential for stable, predictable ranking.

surprises.title: Query sanitizer prevents catastrophic recall cliff from system-prompt contamination
surprises.detail: When AI agents prepend system prompts to search queries (2000+ chars), embedding models represent the concatenated string as a single vector where the prompt dominates the actual question, causing recall to drop from ~90% to 1% silently. The sanitizer's 4-step approach recovers to 70-80% worst-case instead of catastrophic failure.

surprises.title: Dedup is chunk-precise, not file-precise, to allow same-source multi-chunk retrieval
surprises.detail: When merging BM25 and vector candidates, dedup key is (_source_file_full, _chunk_index). A single source file may be split into 10 drawers; BM25 might find chunk 3 (high keyword match) while vector found chunk 7 (high semantic match). Both should be in the rerank pool. File-level dedup would silently drop one; chunk-level dedup lets the same source contribute multiple perspectives.

designDecisions.decision: Hybrid ranking always runs, with vector weighting 60% and BM25 40%.
designDecisions.rationale: Pure vector retrieval fails on exact-match queries (directory listings, diffs, mechanical content that embeds as noise). Pure BM25 misses semantic paraphrases. The 60/40 split favors embedding similarity but gives keyword overlap enough weight to rescue lexical matches. Grounded in the CLAUDE.md design principle: '100% recall is the design requirement' - hybrid is the mechanism.

designDecisions.decision: Closets are a ranking signal, never a filter gate.
designDecisions.rationale: Closets are generated via regex extraction on narrative content, so they can be weak or incomplete. Making them a filter would create a 'weak-closets regression' where poor extraction hides good drawer matches. Signal-only mode means drawers found directly always appear; closets just reorder them. This honors the verbatim-always principle: nothing is ever thrown away.

designDecisions.decision: BM25 corpus is the candidate set itself, not a fixed global corpus.
designDecisions.rationale: Computing IDF over the re-rank pool means each query gets term-discriminativeness scores tuned to its specific context. A term rare in the full palace might be common in the top-30 results; using local IDF makes scoring adaptive. This works well for small pools and is cheaper than maintaining global IDF.

designDecisions.decision: Embedding device is configurable (CPU/CUDA/CoreML/DML) and can fall back gracefully.
designDecisions.rationale: MemPalace must run on laptops without GPU. Requesting an unavailable accelerator logs a warning and falls back to CPU rather than hard-failing, so mining still works. CLAUDE.md principle: 'Local-first by default, never silently use an external API.'

designDecisions.decision: Query sanitization happens before embedding; cleaning is observable in logs but not exposed in the API response.
designDecisions.rationale: When contamination is detected, the sanitizer logs a warning but returns clean_query without changing the caller's view of what was searched. This prevents silent surprises while still rescuing recall. The CLAUDE.md principle 'Verbatim always' is honored: the original query is preserved, the returned results are accurate.

related.why: Benchmarks page documents the 96.6% R@5 baseline, hybrid v4's 98.4% held-out performance, and explains why hybrid beats pure-vector for recall
Searcher depends on embedding.py for device-aware model loading (minilm vs embeddinggemma) and hardware acceleration selection
Temporal knowledge graph provides entity relationships and validity windows that could augment search ranking in future enhancements
Searcher operates on the palace's drawer/closet structure; closets are the index layer that ranks drawer retrieval
AAAK dialect generates closet content via entity/topic extraction, which searcher uses as ranking signal without depending on its lossiness
ChromaDB HNSW and SQLite FTS5 storage power vector candidates and the BM25-only fallback path

searchDoc.title: Search & Retrieval
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace fuses vector semantic search with keyword-based BM25 scoring and optional closet-boosting to approach perfect retrieval, reaching 96.6% R@5 with zero LLM and 98.4% on held-out data through the full hybrid pipeline.
searchDoc.body: MemPalace Search and Retrieval combines vector semantic search with keyword-based BM25 scoring and optional closet-boosting for near-perfect recall. The baseline reaches 96.6% R@5 on LongMemEval with zero LLM, the full hybrid pipeline hits 98.4% R@5 on held-out data, and optional Haiku reranking reaches 100%. The architecture ensures weak semantic matches can be rescued by strong keyword overlap or temporal and preference signals, eliminating the pure-vector cold-retrieval problem. Search runs as a layered pipeline. Vector candidate selection is the floor that always runs: every search begins with drawer-direct vector retrieval through ChromaDB's HNSW index, over-sampling n_results times three candidates before ranking. The query is embedded with the configured model, either minilm or embeddinggemma, compared against all drawer embeddings in the requested wing or room, and candidates are collected with raw cosine distances. Subsequent ranking steps can only reorder, never suppress. If a closets collection exists, the system queries it separately and builds a per-source boost table. The top closet for a source yields a 0.40 distance reduction, the second 0.25, down to 0.04 for rank five, applied only when the closet distance is at or below 1.5. Boosts use the closet's ordinal rank, not absolute distance, because narrative content clusters closet distances in the 1.2 to 1.5 range regardless of match quality. After candidate gathering, hybrid rank applies Okapi-BM25 to the candidate-set text. IDF is computed locally over the candidates themselves, corpus-relative not global, so discriminativeness reflects each term's prevalence within the rerank pool. Vector similarity is computed as max of zero and one minus distance into the zero-to-one range, using absolute distance so adding or removing a candidate cannot reshuffle the others. BM25 is min-max normalized within the pool. The final score is 0.6 times vector similarity plus 0.4 times normalized BM25. Effective distance is clamped to the zero-to-two cosine range to keep boosts monotonic. Before embedding, the query sanitizer strips system-prompt contamination using a four-step fallback: passthrough if under 200 characters, question extraction, tail-sentence extraction, then tail truncation, recovering recall from 1 percent to 70 to 80 percent in worst-case contamination scenarios. Union candidate strategy also pulls BM25-only candidates from SQLite FTS5 and merges them with chunk-precise dedup keyed on source file and chunk index. Drawer-grep enrichment expands closet hits that span multiple chunks. When HNSW is unavailable, a BM25-only SQLite fallback reads from chroma.sqlite3 via the FTS5 trigram index so search never crashes. Closets are a ranking signal, never a filter gate, honoring the verbatim-always principle that nothing is thrown away. Key symbols include search_memories, _hybrid_rank, _bm25_scores, sanitize_query, get_embedding_function, and the CLOSET_RANK_BOOSTS constant.
